This harengon brigand is an insufferable braggart and a daring thief who's willing to put himself in seemingly precarious situations when he has an audience, confident that his speed and cunning will see him through danger. He leads by example rather than by dictate.
"What's yours is mine; it's only a matter of time."
"I have a reputation to uphold. I can't have it sullied by silly concepts like honesty and generosity."
"My confidence is bound up in my scarf's powers. I'm quite the coward without it."
This prince made a bargain with Endelyn Moongrave and is paying the price. He longs to return to his home in the Misty Forest and deal with the threat of an evil green dragon that nests there.
"I am an elf, and time is on my side. I refuse to give up—ever."

"The elves of the Misty Forest will lose their homes and likely perish if that green dragon isn't slain or driven off. I shall deal with the dragon before it visits great harm on the forest and my people. That is what a prince is expected to do."
"Ah, the Misty Forest! No other wood compares to it in beauty and serenity."
"To relent is to show weakness, and I shall not be seen as weak. It is my destiny to be king."
This 3-foot-tall talking dandelion finds poetry in everything and is quick to fall head over heels in love. A humble idealist, Amidor never puts its own needs above the needs of others.

"My speech drifts into flowery verse, if you'll pardon the pun. Allow me to demonstrate: Do not cry, my love! Let me catch your tears as faeries collect morning dew. Let me lift your spirits like a seed on the breeze!"
"The pursuit of true love compels me! Never shall I wilt if I have such a cause to champion."
"I cannot resist a pretty face or a heavenly scent."

s: One of Halaster's apprentices was a human transmuter named Arcturia, who created all manner of new monsters and often made herself the subject of her own horrid magical transformations. She claimed an entire level of Undermountain as her lair and polymorphed prisoners into monsters to guard it. It's likely that Arcturia resides in Undermountain still, in one form or another.

Queen Argantle sports a generous beard and whiskers. Her hair is shorn on one side, from where Endelyn Moongrave recently snipped off the queen's precious, powerful locks. Argantle wears an abundance of shale jewelry that doesn't seem to weigh her down in the least.
"My mood is as stormy as the skies of Yon, and I hurl boulders when I'm angry."
"Bitter End is a raving tyrant. I live in hope that one day we'll be free of that hag."
"I have sworn to protect Lockbury Henge, and I'll defend it with every last whisker."
"I am quick to make enemies and slow to make friends."
The importance of some physical object that must be obtained, protected, or destroyed at all costs

Justice and revenge for great wrongs; those on a quest to rid the world of great evil

Embedded in a mountain south of Phandalin is the ancient dwarven fortress of Axeholm, which has been sealed for years. If a dragon attack is imminent, the people of Phandalin can evacuate and take refuge in Axeholm. To that end, someone needs to open the fortress and make it safe for habitation. Once you accomplish these tasks, return to Townmaster Wester to collect a reward of 250 gp.

Burly and his brother, Hurly, joined the carnival as youngsters. Hurly disappeared a few months ago, and search parties failed to locate him. Mister Witch and Mister Light convinced Burly to stay with the carnival afterward, rather than continue the search on his own. When he's not straining at some feat of athleticism, he's reading books of poetry.
"I treat my brain like a muscle and try to keep it strong."
"I keep the peace. I don't advocate violence; I'm just doing my job."
"After my brother disappeared, everyone in the carnival was so nice to me. I look out for them."
"Sometimes I forget my own strength and accidentally break things. Especially fragile things."

Orcs have attacked Butterskull Ranch, five miles east of Conyberry along the Triboar Trail! Travel there with haste, assess the damage, and help any way you can. Alfonse Kalazorn, the ranch owner, is a retired sheriff who can reward you for your efforts. If he's dead, return to Townmaster Harbin Wester with proof of Kalazorn's demise to receive a reward of 100 gp.
You immediately gain the benefits of finishing a long rest.

Candlefoot's appearance is strangely monochromatic, due to the chaotic magic of a reckless sorcerer to whom he was apprenticed in his youth. After fleeing his master, Candlefoot found a home in the Witchlight Carnival. He can communicate only through mime until his stolen voice is retrieved from the kenku warlock, Kettlesteam.
"I shrug a lot because I'm indecisive."
"Love has the power to conquer all."
"My true love, Palasha, means everything to me. I'd live my life's misfortunes a hundred times over if I knew the path that would lead me back to her."
"I'm afraid of my own reflection and avoid looking into mirrors. The Hall of Illusions terrifies me."

s: This card describes a special charm. Give the card to the player whose character receives the charm. Collect the card when the charm ends for that character.

Chucklehead's real name is Fug. He has a strong affection for Mishka (the only child in Loomlurch who doesn't fear or mock him) and treats her like a younger sibling. He resists any attempt to remove the maggot that lives in his head, because he fears losing it might turn him back into the uncaring, self-serving person he was previously.
"I get angry when people make fun of my head."
"Not all goblins are the same. I mean, look at me."
"Mishka is like my little sister. I don't like how Granny Nightshade treats her."
"The maggot showed me my true self. I'll always love it for that, even as it eats my head."

Despite the loss of its original head, this child-sized scarecrow retains an upbeat demeanor characterized by its affinity for gallows humor. With its long claws and rattling gourd head, Clapperclaw knows it can be off-putting to strangers, and it relies on humor to defuse tension.
"I'm generally positive, and I make jokes when I'm nervous or sense tension in the air."
"I prefer to keep moving from place to place."
"My original head. It was perfect every way. I hope to get it back one day."

s: The DM determines whether anyone involved in the combat encounter is {@status surprised}.

The DM decides where all the characters and monsters are located. Given the character's marching order and their stated positions, the DM figures out where the adversaries are—how far away and in what direction.

When every participant in the combat has had a turn, the round ends. Repeat step 4 until the fighting stops.

s: Granny Nightshade reared Cradlefall from an egg, but the hag's alchemical incubation processes stunted the dragon's growth, making him small even for a wyrmling. Cradlefall is Granny Nightshade's most loyal servant—a slithering parcel of cruelty that's never far from her side.
"I hiss when I speak and slink around whomever I'm talking with."
"Terror is the best teacher, and frightened children make the best workers."
"Skabatha Nightshade is my true, loving mother. I must honor and protect her."
"My words are laced with veiled threats, even when I'm pretending to be nice."

Recent conflicts in Menzoberranzan have left weakened drow houses fearing for their future. Drow are coming to Undermountain in droves to carve out sanctuaries for one house or another. Halaster can't be happy to see them return in force, but who knows? Maybe the Mad Mage orchestrated the upheaval to bring the dark elves scurrying back for reasons beyond the comprehension of the sane.

The Mad Mage has transformed an entire level of Undermountain into a proving ground for adventurers who seek to reach the deepest layers of the dungeon and the treasures hidden within. At the end of this underground obstacle course waits the greatest challenge of all: Netherskull the Death Tyrant, an undead beholder that hates wizards above all.

All that is wrong with government and leadership; those who rule through fear and violence

Dirlagraun was raised by a noble high elf family of the Summer Court and blessed with the ability to speak and understand Common and Sylvan. The displacer beast adores the company of children and served as a nanny to the family's children.
Dirlagraun's own offspring, a kitten named Star, went missing a few weeks ago.
"My tentacles flick in the air when my guard is up."
"Nurture the young, for they are the bright lights of tomorrow."
"I'm duty-bound to protect the young guests of the Witchlight Carnival."
"I can't forgive myself for the disappearance of my cub, Star."
The pursuit of knowledge tempered by wisdom; truth and honesty; sages and prophecy

Isolation and imprisonment; being so conservative in thinking as to be a prisoner of one's own beliefs
Donnabella is a young magic-user who wears a papier-mâché unicorn mask because it makes her feel more magical.
Use the {@creature Spellcaster|ESK} sidekick stat block to represent her.
"I'd rather talk to a book than most people."
"We all have a little magic in us. The trick is finding it and bringing it forth."
"I want to join a prestigious wizards' academy one day. I just hope they accept unicorns!"
"I can't keep a secret to save my life—or anyone else's."

Jingle Jangle is a kind soul who refers to herself in the third person. She has a knack for finding keys and is thrilled to add new ones to her collection. She also gives keys as gifts to those who need them.
Jingle Jangle seeks a quiet life far away from locked doors and the intrigues of the fey courts. She moved to Telemy Hill to enjoy the hill's companionship and protection.
"Jingle Jangle is thorough and fastidious. No cutting corners."
"Revel in your uniqueness, whether you're a goblin who likes keys or an awakened hill with talking trees."
"Jingle Jangle keeps her keys shiny and clean."
"Jingle Jangle is frightened by locked doors!"
Our capability to discern what is truly important and to use it to weed the garden of our life.

You momentarily gain the ability to balance the scales of fate. For the next 8 hours, whenever you or a creature within 60 feet of you is about to roll a {@dice d20} with advantage or disadvantage, you can use your reaction to prevent the roll from being affected by advantage or disadvantage.
Your capacity to create a new reality through shattering old, limiting beliefs.

Kettlesteam delights in causing trouble at the carnival. She uses a combination of mimicry and conjured illusions to communicate; she has overheard so many conversations that she can talk in one of several different voices.
"I'm stubborn as a dog gnawing a bone (mimics the sound of a dog gnawing a bone)."
"Malicious joy. I can't help but chuckle when people mess up (mimics the sound of someone stumbling and others laughing)."
"I have a fey pact with Zybilna of Prismeer (mimics the sound of the wind blowing through willows and faraway tinkling bells)."
"I have a volatile temper (mimics the sound of a kettle boiling over)."
A rare or rarer magic weapon with which you are proficient appears in your hands. The DM chooses the weapon.
A person with the skills or tools needed to solve the current problem.
A creature that preys on the party's weaknesses, or a trap that can be disarmed only with a key.
A place through which only certain people are allowed to pass, or where a key is required.

An open and easily accessed place.
A treasure in a locked container, or magic that slows creatures.
A situation that can be successfully resolved in many ways.

A rare or rarer magic weapon with which you are proficient appears in your hands. The DM chooses the weapon.

A common or uncommon magic weapon with which you are proficient, or a {@item spell scroll} featuring a spell of a level you can cast, appears in your hands. The DM chooses the weapon or spell, which you possess for the duration of this adventure.
Reaping the fruits of your endeavours. Enjoying abundance while not getting lost in acquiring.
Using the panels of your intellect clearly without letting it override your heart.
Fully expressing your powers of leadership and realising your vision. Teaching others.
Fully accepting this moment. Allowing complaints to dissolve. Being kind to yourself.
An uncommon magic weapon you're proficient with appears in your hands. The DM chooses the weapon.
This card creates an illusion of a {@creature Knight|XMM}.

You gain the service of a 4th-level fighter who appears in a space you choose within 30 feet of you. The fighter is of the same race as you and serves you loyally until death, believing the fates have drawn him or her to you. You control this character.
A trustworthy person who honors their commitments.
A creature bound by oaths or who serves someone else.
A place of sanctuary, where strong traditions protect those who take shelter inside.
A treasure celebrating or commemorating an oath (such as a wedding ring), or magic weapons or armor associated with knights or paladins.
A situation that requires loyalty in one's companions and faithfulness to them.
A person who can't be trusted, or a traitor posing as a loyal friend.
A knight who has failed to live up to their code of honor (such as a {@creature death knight}).
A place where a great betrayal took place, or a location with treacherous terrain or traps.
A treasure that carries a hidden curse, or a magic item that fails when it's needed most.
A situation involving the betrayal of trust, or rampant suspicion.

As an action, you can throw this card to an unoccupied space on the ground within 60 feet of yourself while speaking a command word, whereupon the card magically transforms into a {@creature deck defender|BMT} (see {@book chapter 9|BMT|8|Deck Defender} for its stat block) for up to 1 minute or until you use an action to speak the command word again, whereupon it transforms back into a card. The deck defender obeys your spoken commands. If you issue no commands, it takes the {@action Dodge} action and moves to avoid danger. The deck defender reverts to a card early if it drops to 0 hit points. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

You gain the service of a 4th-level fighter who appears in a space you choose within 30 feet of you. The fighter is of the same race as you and serves you loyally until death, believing the fates have drawn him or her to you. You control this character.

You gain the service of a {@creature Knight|XMM}, who magically appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 30 feet of yourself. The knight has the same alignment as you and serves you loyally until death, believing the two of you have been drawn together by fate. Work with your DM to create a name and backstory for this NPC. The DM can use a different stat block to represent the knight, as desired.

You gain the service of any of the NPCs in the "{@book Hirelings|phb|5|services}" section not currently with the party, who appears in a space you choose within 30 feet of you. The NPC serves you loyally for the duration of the adventure, believing that the fates have drawn them to you. You control this character.

s: Finding a way to enjoy routine, take responsibility for our own success, and let go of expectations. Good work speaks for itself.
Channelling raw ambition into a constructive thoughtful and focused plan.
Going full out and not looking back. Following your gut. Doing what it takes to make it happen.
Trusting your passion, allowing yourself to dream big, and imagining the best happening for you.
This card creates an illusion of a {@creature Kobold Warrior|XMM}.
The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or suffer the effect of a {@spell confusion} spell with a duration of 1 minute.
When the target rolls damage, it can reroll any of the damage dice once. It must use the new rolls, after which this boon effect ends.
Kubazan the {@creature Froghemoth|VGM}, is wild and spirited.
While inhabited by Kubazan, you gain the following flaw, which overrides any opposing flaw: "I am fearless and not afraid to take great risks."
While Kubazan inhabits you, your Strength score becomes 23 unless it is already higher.
The target must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 10d10} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful save.

The target gains a pool of ten {@dice d6|d6s}. Up to two of these dice can be expended at a time and added to any damage roll the target makes when it hits with a weapon attack. The damage added by these dice is fire damage.
For the next 24 hours, the target can't gain advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, or saving throws.
Once within the next 24 hours, the target can use its reaction to reduce the damage it takes from one source by {@dice 10d6}.
All your ability scores increase by 1, to a maximum of 20.
A surgeon, or someone (such as a guard or soldier) who uses violence in pursuit of worthy societal goals.
A creature trained to fight alongside guards or soldiers.
A place where surgery is performed.
A treasure made at great cost, or a magic weapon.
A situation in which additional pain is required to bring healing.
A person committed to pacifism or avoiding harm,
A creature uninterested in fighting, or a trap that restrains but doesn't cause damage.
A place where violence is forbidden.
A treasure celebrating the end of hostilities or the ideal of peace, or a magic item intended to prevent or end conflict.
A situation complicated by people avoiding any hint of conflict.
This card creates an illusion of a {@creature Lich|XMM}.
You gain the ability to cast {@spell Knock} {@dice 1d3} times. Use your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as the spellcasting ability (your choice).

Deep in Neverwinter Wood, along the river that flows west toward Neverwinter, is a logging camp. Every two months, Phandalin delivers fresh supplies to the camp, which is run by the half-brother of Phandalin's townmaster, Harbin Wester. Barthen, the local provisioner, has prepared a new delivery. He needs someone to bear the supplies safely to the camp. Return to Harbin Wester with a notice of delivery signed by his half-brother, Tibor Wester, to claim your reward of 100 gp.
{@note Specifically a {@item lute|PHB} in this instance.}

The Shadowdusks were a Waterdavian noble family whose quest for political supremacy ended centuries ago after Shadowdusk wizards opened portals to the Far Realm. Twisted by madness and driven from their home, they sought assistance from Halaster and sank into the depths of Undermountain, never to be seen again—yet vestiges of the noble house undoubtedly remain.
Your Intelligence score increases by 2, to a maximum of 22.
A person (perhaps a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard) who uses arcane magic or other specialized learning.
A creature with abilities similar to those of a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard.
A place dedicated to the study of arcane magic or that is suffused with such magic.
A magic item such as a wand or staff, or a wizard's spellbook.
A situation that requires and rewards the correct use of arcane magic.
A person who wrongly believes their good luck is the result of innate magical ability or a magical good luck charm.
A creature that resists or negates magic.
A place where magic has caused destruction, doesn't work (like the effect of an {@spell Antimagic Field}), or works unpredictably (perhaps triggering {@table Wild Magic Surge|PHB|wild magic surges}).
An art object created by the use of magic, or a magic item with unpredictable effects (such as a {@item Wand of Wonder}).
A situation caused by magic misused or out of control.

At any time you choose within 1 year of drawing this card, you can mentally name or describe an object or individual that is familiar to you. You immediately know the location of the object or individual, as well as the distance between you and the object or individual, even if the object or individual is on a different plane of existence. If you named an individual, you know if they are alive and any conditions they have. If you named an object, you know if it is broken or not. If you named a magic item that has charges, you know how many charges it has remaining.
A person who acts as a guide, showing the way forward.
A creature that tracks by scent.
A valuable map (perhaps a jeweled globe or rare atlas), or a magic item that provides direction.
A situation best navigated with a guide.
Someone who tries to lead you on the wrong path.
A creature (such as a {@creature will-o'-wisp}) that leads travelers astray.
A demiplane or similar place that can't be found on maps, or a location hidden behind a secret door.
A treasure from another plane of existence, or a magic item that creates or accesses an extradimensional space (like a {@item Portable Hole}).
No guide or direction is available.
The presence of a spy or a minion of some greater power; an encounter with a puppet or an underling
A person who feels lost in their own life, unsure how to affect change, or a person with a wandering mind who takes their time getting to the point.
A minotaur or another creature that hunts in a maze or is imprisoned in a maze.
A maze, or a region (such as a forest or desert) where becoming lost is very easy.
An art object depicting confusion or disorientation, or a magic item that can cause these states.
A confusing situation where it's difficult to perceive all the factors at play.
A person running from expectations placed on them by family and society, trying to find a new path in life.
A creature whose behavior is unpredictable.
A simple labyrinth designed for meditation or to provide private nooks, or a location in which one is unlikely to get lost (such as a cave with only one exit).
An art object incorporating a labyrinth design.
A search for something or someone that has gone missing.

Inner strength and fortitude; those who fight for power or wealth
A rare commodity or business opportunity; deceitful or dangerous business transactions
A pile of {@dice 2d6} gems (each worth 5,000 gp) and {@dice 1d10} chunks of precious ore (each worth 2,500 gp) appears at your feet.
A creature that burrows underground, especially one that delves into the earth in search of prey (such as a {@creature giant weasel}).
A mine, an archaeological dig, or a similar excavated site.
A treasure from the earth, such as metal ore or gems, or any treasure that has been buried and unearthed.
Something unearthed that should have remained buried.
Someone who places things in the earth, such as a gardener or an undertaker.
A creature that lives underground but hunts above ground (such as an {@creature ankheg} or a {@creature bulette}).
A place that has sunk into the earth, perhaps swallowed in a sinkhole or covered in a mudslide.
A treasure buried in the earth.
You receive an uncommon wondrous item (chosen by the DM), or you can draw two additional cards beyond your declared draws.
Hoarded wealth; those who are irreversibly unhappy or who think money is meaningless
Those who spread wisdom and faith to others; warnings of the spread of fear and ignorance
Mister Light is the face of the Witchlight Carnival. He's a loud, flamboyant ringleader who'll do anything to maintain the carnival's happy atmosphere.
Mister Light wears a harlequin suit and a jaunty hat. When he presides over the carnival's Big Top, he sparkles like a disco ball.
"There's always something for me to smile about."
"Delight. I want everyone to feel the wonder that I feel each day in this place."
"Mister Witch is my greatest friend and most trusted confidant."
"I was the crueler of the two of us, long ago. Perhaps that streak of violence hasn't quite left me."
Mister Witch is businesslike and humorless as he deals with staff and keeps the carnival running on schedule. A smile on his visage is a rare event, and it fades quickly.
Mister Witch dresses with panache, though in muted tones, and always carries his magic pocket watch.
"I carefully consider my words before speaking them aloud."
"Caution. Thoughtless decisions lead to reckless acts."
"This carnival is our opportunity for a new life, far away from the gloomy world we came from."
"I'm too confident in my own authority to see the seeds of doubt in the carnival staff."
Something unexpected or mysterious that can't be avoided; a great quest or journey that will try one's spirit
Moa the {@creature Jaculi|ToA}, is truthful and kind.
While inhabited by Moa, you gain the following flaw, which overrides any opposing flaw: "I must always speak the truth."

While inhabited by Moa, you can use an action to turn {@condition invisible}. Anything you are wearing or carrying is invisible as long as it is on your person. The effect ends if you attack, cast a spell, force a saving throw, or deal damage.
Serenity; inner strength and self-reliance; supreme confidence bereft of arrogance

This card's monstrous visage curses you. While cursed in this way, whenever you make a saving throw, you must roll {@dice 1d4} and subtract the number rolled from the total. The curse lasts until you finish a long rest, but it can be ended early with a {@spell Remove Curse} spell or similar magic.

A {@filter Large or larger Monstrosity with a challenge rating of 10 or less|bestiary|source=|Challenge Rating=[&0;&10]|type=monstrosity|size=l;h;g} (chosen by the DM) appears in an unoccupied space within 15 feet of you. The creature is hostile toward you and attacks immediately. The creature disappears when it is killed or when you are reduced to 0 hit points. If there isn't enough space for a Large or larger creature to appear, this card has no effect.
A familiar person whose behavior suddenly turns threatening.
A Monstrosity, especially one that superficially resembles an ordinary animal or person (such as a {@creature displacer beast} or {@creature doppelganger}).
A familiar place that has become dangerous.
An art object depicting a Monstrosity or that incorporates claws, fur, or feathers from such a creature.
A situation involving something or someone becoming more monstrous (literally or figuratively).
A person who seems dangerous or bizarre but is friendly and helpful.
A Monstrosity that is a potential ally, such as a {@creature hippogriff}.
A place that offers refuge in unfamiliar or dangerous terrain.
A dead Monstrosity preserved by taxidermy, or a magic item useful against Monstrosities.
Something that appears monstrous but is actually benign.
You are granted the ability to cast the {@spell wish} spell {@dice 1d3} times.
Someone whose fine qualities are masked by one annoying trait.
A lycanthrope, or a creature that appears to be an inanimate object until it strikes (such as a {@creature gargoyle}).
A secret chamber or a place concealed by terrain; alternatively, a place larger or more elaborate on the inside than it seems from outside.
A treasure whose value isn't immediately apparent, or a magic item that appears to be a worthless object.
A problem that requires investigation and is more complicated than it appears.
A person who seems competent but bungles everything they attempt.
A creature that uses its fearsome appearance to frighten away others because it is too weak to fight.
A place with an impressive exterior but a dingy, poorly maintained interior.
A treasure that seems more valuable than it is, perhaps an ordinary item that falsely appears magical.
A situation that seems—and is—too good to be true.

As an action, you can speak a command word while touching this card and transform into a wolflike biped for 1 minute. For that duration, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and when you hit a target with a weapon or an unarmed strike, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} force damage. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.
You are granted the ability to cast the {@spell wish} spell {@dice 1d3} times.
You gain the ability to cast {@spell Wish|XPHB} {@dice 1d3} times.
You are granted the ability to cast any spell of 5th level or lower, and can use that ability {@dice 1d3} times for the duration of the adventure.

s: The Knight of Warts is known for her skill at piloting balloons. Justice and moral clarity guide her every action. Despite being held prisoner for treason, she claims that her honor remains intact. Even if it means losing her title, she refuses to bow to King Gullop XIX or renounce her friend and companion, Wigglewog, with whom she conspired to help Sir Talavar escape Bavlorna's clutches.
"I spit whenever I hear a coward or a liar speak."
"Honor is what makes a knight, even beyond duty or prowess with a weapon."
"Ballooning. There's nothing quite like taking flight in a balloon and going where the winds take you."
"I'm a snob who criticizes the state and quality of weapons wielded by others."

The Mountain's Toe Gold Mine lies fifteen miles northeast of Phandalin. The new overseer, Don-Jon Raskin, just made the trip from Neverwinter to Phandalin and needs to be escorted to the mine. There's no telling what dangers lie between here and there. Once you deliver Raskin safe and sound, return to Townmaster Harbin Wester to collect a reward of 100 gp.
Great heroes; a sudden reversal of fate; the triumph of the underdog over a mighty enemy
You have disadvantage on Intelligence saving throws for 1 hour. Discard this card and draw from the deck again; together, the two draws count as one of your declared draws.
Nangnang the {@creature Grung|VGM}, is selfish and cruel.
While inhabited by Nangnang, you gain the following flaw, which overrides any opposing flaw: "I won't share with others."

While inhabited by Nangnang, you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, while leaving your hands free. You also gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.

The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition incapacitated} for 1 hour. While {@condition incapacitated} in this way, the target gains the following personality flaw, which supersedes any opposing flaw: "I fundamentally disagree with everything anyone else says."
The target can cast the {@spell augury} spell as an action three times, requiring no components and with no chance of a random reading.
Unnatural events and unhealthy obsessions; those who follow a destructive path

Halaster brought seven apprentices with him to Undermountain. One of them, Nester, became a lich using spells and methods of his own devising. But his process was flawed, and over time Nester's phylactery and body disintegrated until only his floating skull and skeletal arms remained. Driven mad by his failure to achieve true lichdom, Nester continues to haunt Undermountain in this weakened form.

s: Nib is a happy-go-lucky gambler who keeps a deck of Three-Dragon Ante cards in her vest pocket. She also has a goldfinch named Lil.
Use the {@creature Spellcaster|ESK} sidekick stat block to represent her.
"I can't resist a sure bet or a friendly wager."
"The more complicated the scheme, the better."
"I love birds and will do what I can to look after them."
"Deep water terrifies me. I would rather be swallowed by a dragon than get in a boat or go for a swim."

Nib (whose real name is Meryl Caberstock) is a tall, rake-thin, elderly man dressed in threadbare finery and a housecoat. He wears a blindfold to avoid glimpsing the apparitions that curse him, but their presence still unnerves him.
"I speak in a trembling voice and jump at the slightest shadow."
"I seek atonement. I was the worst of Waterdeep's slumlords: ruthless, miserly, and cold-hearted. I suppose I'd better do some good before I die."
"My spinning wheel is the key to my redemption."
"Yes, I'm scared. If you'd done all the things I've done, you'd be scared too."
You gain {@sense darkvision} within a range of 300 feet. This {@sense darkvision} lasts for 8 hours.

You will go ninth in the initiative order.
The capability to come out of "survival mode" and enjoy the abundance and self-sufficiency that we do have. Appreciate the good.
Looking at how thoughts can create turmoil and finding a way to observe them from a dispassionate space of stillness.
Finding the wellspring of resolve to push through hardship. A test of faith.
Finding the balance between enjoying our accomplishments and not slipping into complacency.

Northwind embodies the joys of spring, finding childlike wonder in everything from a story told by a stranger to a drop of morning dew. The sapling hails from a line of Feywild treants and travels as the Witchlight Carnival's landscaper, laying down silk ribbons to form rivers and planting acorns that grow rapidly into splendid oak trees.
"I love to hear stories. Tell me everything!"
"Joy. Just look at the world around us! Isn't it amazing?"
"My ancestors. One day I will grow into an enormous tree and they will be so proud!"
"Oops! I simply cannot keep a secret."
Obo'laka the {@creature Zorbo|ToA}, is nervous and obsessive.
While inhabited by Obo'laka, you gain the following flaw, which overrides any opposing flaw: "I am risk-averse and a slave to routine."
While Obo'laka inhabits you, you can attune to one additional magic item. When Obo'laka leaves you, all magic items to which you are attuned are no longer attuned to you.

A {@creature gelatinous cube} immediately appears in your space and engulfs you. The gelatinous cube is hostile and remains until it is destroyed. If there isn't enough space for the gelatinous cube to appear, this card has no effect.
A quiet, unassuming person who has hidden power or secret knowledge.
An Ooze or another creature that seems unimportant, or a trap that is surprisingly simple and straightforward.
A humble place of surprising comfort or importance.
A treasure that is valuable but not beautiful, such as a poorly crafted piece of jewelry incorporating precious stones.
Something important that has been overlooked because it seems ordinary.
A quiet, unassuming person completely out of their depth.

A situation complicated by the sheer number of minor factors tangled within it.
You gain resistance to one of the following damage types (chosen by the DM): force, necrotic, poison, psychic, or radiant. This resistance lasts for {@dice 1d12} days.
Getting into action and rekindling a sense of adventure with even the small things. Realize what isn't working.
Discovering new ways of communicating your ideas and putting them into action.
It takes energy to do something awesome. Go for it! Engage your free spirit and follow your passion.
Embarking on a new path sparked by your curiosity and creativity.
Just and noble warriors; those who live by a code of honor and integrity

Palasha is an elegant and operatic mermaid whose long fins billow even when she's not underwater. She sculpts water with her extraordinary voice, creating astounding displays of aquatic magic. Palasha's distant yet demanding nature has earned her a reputation for being haughty, but really, she's just slow to trust.
"I click my fingers at those around me when I want something."
"I strive to bring beauty and wonder into this world with the power of my voice."
"Candlefoot. I can be myself around him."
"I have trouble showing my true feelings, which makes me seem aloof."
Papazotl the {@creature Eblis|ToA}, is shrewd and conniving.
While inhabited by Papazotl, you gain the following flaw, which overrides any opposing flaw: "I bow before no one and expect others to do as I command."
While inhabited by Papazotl, you can't be surprised, you gain advantage on all Wisdom checks, and you never take damage from falling.
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
A goal-oriented person who knows exactly what they want and has a clear plan to get it.
A creature single-mindedly pursuing prey or some other goal, or a trapped room navigable by only a single path.
An art object depicting a road or path, or a magic item that allows divination (such as a {@item Crystal Ball} or a {@item Spell Scroll (6th Level)|DMG|Spell Scroll} of {@spell Find the Path}).
A situation that demands unwavering focus on the goal.
An aimless person who doesn't know what they want and has no idea how to decide.
A creature that reacts to provocation without a clear plan or purpose; it might be acting on instinct or be confused.
A trackless wilderness, or an underground complex that is very difficult to traverse.
An abstract art object, or a magic item that foils divination (such as an {@item Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location}).
A series of distractions that deflect attention from an important goal.
Charity and giving on a grand scale; those who use wealth to fight evil and sickness
Pete likes ale and tends to function better while tipsy. At his best, he's quite the handyman and comes up with all sorts of crazy ways to get things done.
Use the {@creature Expert|esk} sidekick stat block to represent him.
"My friends know they can rely on me, no matter what."
"I like coming up with new ways to do things. What problem can't be solved with a little ingenuity?"
"A full flask of wine is worth ten pockets full of gold."
"All this drinking is bad for my memory. Seriously, I can't remember my last name."

Pincushion is Skabatha Nightshade's childhood doll—an animated nanny brought to life by Baba Yaga to help educate Skabatha. The doll's magic has kept it well preserved, despite its great age. Granny Nightshade has put Pincushion in charge of producing fabric for her toy workshop—a job the doll considers beneath it.
"I behave like the conceited mistress of a high-society fashion house."
"I want Skabatha to respect all I've done for her."
"Nobody knows more about fashion than I do."
A pit opens beneath you. You plummet {@damage 3d6 × 10} feet, take damage from the fall, and have the {@condition prone} condition.
A person who has lost significant wealth, social status, or favor.
A pit trap, or a scavenger lurking at the bottom of a pit.
A pit or cliff that creates the risk of a fall.
An art object depicting someone's calamitous fall, or a magic item that allows falling safely (such as a {@item Ring of Feather Falling}).
A situation involving someone's fall from grace.
A person in a precarious position who soon will have a calamitous fall.
A creature (such as a {@creature piercer}) that attacks by falling on prey.
An abandoned mansion or palace that is in disrepair due to the owner's downfall.
An art object depicting flight or incorporating feathers, or a magic item that grants flight (such as {@item Winged Boots} or a {@item Cloak of the Bat}).
A conspiracy to cause the downfall of a wealthy or prominent person.

You gain the ability to cast {@spell Speak with Plants} without using a spell slot; you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. If you have spell slots of 3rd level or higher, you can cast this spell using them. Use your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as the spellcasting ability (your choice).
A person who lives in the wilderness among trees and other growing things.
A Plant creature, or a creature that facilitates the growth of wild plants.
A verdant place where vegetation grows wild, untouched by people's hands.
An art object crafted from wood or incorporating leaves; alternatively, a magic item that allows uncontrolled vegetation growth (such as a {@item Bag of Beans}).
Something growing out of control with surprising, even supernatural, speed.
A quiet person who enjoys gardening or farming, finding greenery more relatable than people.
A domesticated plant given artificial animation, such as an {@creature awakened tree} or {@creature awakened shrub|MM|shrub}.
A place full of carefully pruned and neatly controlled vegetation, such as a topiary garden.

Secret temples exist in great numbers in Undermountain, particularly those of evil gods not welcomed in the city above. The vile servants of these deities are locked in an endless war for supremacy in the dark dungeon. Lolth, the Demon Queen of Spiders, is the fiendish mastermind behind many of these bloody conflicts.

Our capacity to deal with something in a measured and patient way.

A deity or entity of similar power becomes bound to aid you. At any point in time between drawing the card and when you die, you can use your action to call on this entity for divine intervention, and the entity is bound to answer. The parameters and nature of this intervention are chosen by the DM. If you die without having used this intervention, the deity fulfills its obligation by casting the {@spell Resurrection} spell on you. Once the entity has answered your call for divine intervention or resurrected you, the entity is no longer bound to aid you.

A temple guardian—perhaps a Celestial, Construct, or {@creature guardian naga}.

The security that comes with having a network of people who support you and your dreams. Long-term success.
How we deal with what shows up in our lives. Do we avoid and deny? Do we react in anger? Do we remain conscious and aware?
Making sure to speak up. Don't try to do it all. Delegate responsibility where you can. Express yourself.
Uniting the head and the heart. Relating to others and your environment in emotional balance.

Thaco is the longest-serving Witchlight hand, but no one really knows his history and scarcely any dare to ask, for he almost never speaks and harbors a malicious streak that is kept in check by Mister Witch. He paints his face with a grin and puffs on a bubble pipe. Thaco has retired from performing and no longer stages his knife-throwing act due to an unfortunate incident that took place in the Big Top some time ago.
"I prefer not to talk. When I must, I say as little as possible."
"My bubble pipe—if anyone touches it, they lose a finger."
"I can't stand children. They're like roaches."

Following through on your intentions and manifesting your desires.

Finding the source of your inner authority.
Realizing your capacity to express beauty and to nurture others from a place of power.

Returning to the innocence and vitality of childhood.

The collapse of beliefs or material structures that we hold dear. It is in the nonresistance where we can find peace and wisdom.

A turning point in your destiny and your ability to adapt to change.
Endings. Coming to a place of completion and power internally and externally.
Those who steal or burgle; a loss of property, beauty, innocence, friendship, or reputation

Zybilna's butler appears as a lanky man clad in faded brown clothes. Thinnings longs to see Prismeer's archfey freed from temporal stasis and her enemies fed their comeuppance. He helps anyone whose goals align with his own, but he abhors violence and shuns combat.
"Hospitality, ownership, reciprocity—the rules of conduct must be respected."
"I have pledged my fealty to Zybilna of Prismeer, and I am nothing if not her loyal servant."
"Don't expect me to come to your rescue. I didn't get this far by being brave or foolhardy."

Using the power of a team and learning how to collaborate.
Finding a way to heal and learn from anxiety and emotional pain.
Expanding your circle of influence and communicating your ideas. Making progress
Taking time to celebrate the simple joy of aliveness with your friends.

Trobriand was one of Halaster's most promising and demented apprentices. Fascinated by machines, he carved out a level of the Mad Mage's dungeon for himself and set to work building an army of constructs there. It is said that Trobriand controls his creations with a metal ring, and that he crafted similar rings of lesser power for his apprentices, to protect them in the event that his constructs went insane.

The local midwife—an acolyte of {@deity Chauntea|Faerûnian|SCAG} named Adabra Gwynn—lives by herself in a stone windmill on the side of a hill a few miles south of Phandalin. With dragon sightings becoming common, it's not safe for her to be alone. Urge Adabra to return to Phandalin. Once she's safe, visit Townmaster Harbin Wester to claim a reward of 25 gp.

The River of the Depths connects the fourth and fifth levels of Undermountain, skirting the edges of vast caverns filled with trees, shrubs, birds, other animals, and sunlight. An entire forest, as real as any found on the surface, waits to be explored, but an archdruid protects it. And explorers traveling downriver have seen a huge green dragon as well, perched on a tower near a bridge that spans the river.
Unkh the {@creature Flail Snail|VGM}, is self-absorbed and indecisive.
While inhabited by Unkh, you gain the following flaw, which overrides any opposing flaw: "I am incapable of making decisions."
While Unkh inhabits you, your Constitution score becomes 23 unless it is already higher.

The satyr Vansel is a vagabond who travels the Feywild in a constant state of amusement at whatever befalls him. He enjoys bathing and splashing in water, picking flowers, and eating wild mushrooms. He has no shame with regard to who he is and what he looks like, and he has a knack for small talk, reveling in the opportunity to chat with anyone about anything.
"There's fun and delight to be found in every experience."
"Wonders abound in the Feywild, and I would never dream of leaving it."
"I laugh in the face of danger, often to my detriment."

At any time you choose within one year of drawing this card, you can ask a question in meditation and mentally receive a truthful answer to that question. Besides information, the answer helps you solve a puzzling problem or other dilemma. In other words, the knowledge comes with wisdom on how to apply it.

Part of Undermountain was carved out by the drow. Muiral, said to be a former bodyguard and apprentice of Halaster's, claims this domain and hunts trespass- ers for sport. These halls are littered with the bones of the slaughtered. Even the dark elves speak of Muiral in hushed tones. Anyone who can terrify the drow should be avoided at all costs.

Will looks like an 11-year-old lad dressed in a homemade tunic and a spider silk cloak. He is the polymorphed form of an oni named Mugan, who served Granny Nightshade until a curse changed his alignment from lawful evil to chaotic good. Will's time in the forests of Thither has imbued him with a personality common among fairykind: boastful, impulsive, and full of mirth.
"I like to strike a different pose with every sentence I speak."
"Every child must dash free and wild, like me!"
"For the Getaway Gang to flourish, we need more members. Not adults, mind you, just kids like me!"
"I'm as stubborn and slippery as a toad. I won't and I shan't, but I will if I can't!"
Mystery and riddles; the unknown; those who crave magical power and great knowledge
Wongo the {@creature Su-monster|ToA}, is violent and deranged.

While inhabited by Wongo, you can use your action to unleash a psionic assault on a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition stunned} until the end of its next turn.

s: The orcs have fallen under the sway of evil spellcasters in Neverwinter Wood and have been sighted in growing numbers near Falcon's Hunting Lodge. The spellcasters dwell in a ruined manse. Falcon needs someone to make a preemptive strike against it. Destroy the evil in the manse, then expect him to reward you.
This card creates an illusion of a {@creature Wyvern|XMM}.

Iggwilv was a brilliant, calculating figure hardly prone to emotional outbursts, but as Zybilna, she allows her emotions to run rampant and is more likely to find herself in the grip of happiness, anger, or melancholy. This is the price she pays to exert control over the Feywild and impose her will on the domain of Prismeer.
"I have become more temperamental in my old age."
"I used to believe that emotions and kindness were signs of weakness. Now I see their strength."
"My mother, Baba Yaga, warned me that arrogance would be my undoing, 'as sure as stars light the night sky.' She might be right."
